Senses.Explanation: An imperative: 'put it down' or 'set it down,' with the final graph marking the command. The records use it for things held in the hands and for what a questioner says cannot be brought. When a monk raises his sitting cloth and asks for an answer, the teacher says, 'Put it down,' then says 'withdraw' when the monk starts to spread it. In the Yan Yang–Zhaozhou case, Yan Yang asks what to do when not one thing is brought; Zhaozhou says, 'Put it down.' When Yan Yang asks what there is to put down, Zhaozhou replies, 'If you cannot put it down, carry it away.' A second recorded exchange has Shakyamuni tell the Black-Clan Brahmin three times to put things down: first each flower, then, after both hands are empty, the six external objects, six internal faculties, and six intervening discriminations. Another exchange draws the text's own contrast: scattered thoughts are answered with 'put it down,' while not producing a single thought is answered with 'raise it up.' The phrase is an instruction within these specific exchanges; the entry preserves the imperative and its stated objects.
Senses.Note: The exact form has 340 matches in 126 files. The graph variant with the shorter form of the final character has nine matches in five files. The Yan Yang question 'when not one thing is brought' occurs eighty-four times in fifty-four files, and its follow-up 'since not one thing is brought' occurs fourteen times in fourteen. 'Put everything down at once' occurs five times in three files, while the direct opposite imperative 'raise it up' occurs once. None of the seven required definition formulas occurs, so the entry is built from complete exchanges, physical deployments, the text-drawn opposition, and later quotations of the case.

Occurrences.Kwic: 豈不聞昔有僧問趙州：一物不將來時如何？州曰：放下著。僧曰：一物不將來，放下箇甚麼？州曰：放不下，擔取去。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A later address quotes the Yan Yang–Zhaozhou case: Yan Yang asks, 'What about when not one thing is brought?' Zhaozhou answers, 'Put it down.' Yan Yang asks, 'When not one thing is brought, what is there to put down?' Zhaozhou replies, 'If you cannot put it down, carry it away.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 佛曰。放下著。梵志遂放下左手一株華。佛又召仙人。放下著。梵志又放下右手一株華。佛又召仙人。放下著。梵志曰。世尊。我今兩手皆空。更教放下箇甚麼。佛曰。吾非教汝放捨其華。汝當放捨外六塵．內六根．中六識。一時捨却。無可捨處。是汝免生死處。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Five Lamps records Shakyamuni telling the Black-Clan Brahmin, 'Put it down.' The Brahmin puts down the flower in his left hand; at a second command he puts down the flower in his right. At the third command he says both hands are empty and asks what more to put down. Shakyamuni says he is not telling him to discard the flowers, but to discard at once the six external objects, six internal faculties, and six intervening discriminations, until there is no place of discarding; the record calls this his place of escaping birth and death.

Occurrences.Kwic: 又僧出眾，提起坐具，曰：請師答話。師曰：放下著。僧又作展勢，師曰：收。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A monk comes out of the assembly, raises his sitting cloth, and asks the teacher to answer. The teacher says, 'Put it down.' When the monk starts to spread it, the teacher says, 'Withdraw.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 恒鑒問云：「雜念紛飛時如何？」師云：「放下著。」進云：「一念不生時如何？」師云：「提起著。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Hengjian asks, 'What about when miscellaneous thoughts fly about?' The teacher answers, 'Put it down.' Hengjian continues, 'What about when not one thought is produced?' The teacher answers, 'Raise it up.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 但請一時放下著。當人本體自周圓。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui says, 'I ask only that you put everything down at once; the person's own basic substance is complete of itself.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰：向上還有事也無？師曰：放下著。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A monk asks, 'Further above, is there still anything going on or not?' The teacher answers, 'Put it down.'

Senses.Explanation: Literally, 'release' or 'let pass': to permit free movement rather than hold fast. The allowlisted record has 1,034 occurrences in 224 texts. Its recurrent formal counterpart is 'hold fast' (把定) or 'hold in place' (把住): one address says, 'holding fast: dripping water freezes and the rivers stop; releasing: the sun is warm, the wind mild, and the mountains and streams compete in beauty' (把定也，滴水滴凍，江河絕流；放行也，日暖風和，山川競秀), then asks which is good. Other records pair 'release' with 'draw back in' (收來) and use the compact binome 'drawing in and releasing' (收放). The term occurs as a finite verb, in the question 'what is a saying of release?' (如何是放行一句), in the phrase 'open a road of release' (放行一路), and in paired formulas such as 'holding fast and releasing' (把定放行). The texts give different recorded clauses under the two headings; this entry reports that deployment and does not assign a force beyond the words used.
Senses.Note: Corpus counts: 1,034 hits in 224 texts. Attested formations include 'release, then...' (放行則), 151 hits in 80 texts; 'drawing in and releasing' (收放), 310 in 143; 'holding fast and releasing' (把定放行), 15 in 13; 'a road of release' (放行一路), 7 in 6; 'what is release...?' (如何是放行), 11 in 11; and 'not release' (不放行), 40 in 36. No exact definitional formula of the forms 'X means release' or 'is called release' was found. The two hits for 'one who releases' (放行者) are predicative uses, not definitions.

Occurrences.Kwic: 把定也，滴水滴凍，江河絕流；放行也，日暖風和，山川競秀。且道把定好？放行好？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The governing head is the section for Tianzhang Yuanshan (越州天章元善禪師) in the Continuation of the Lamp from the Jianzhong Jingguo Era (建中靖國續燈錄). The address itself supplies the paired clauses and asks whether holding fast or releasing is good. The roster has no exact linkable spelling for this master, so MasterName is null.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如來正法眼藏委在今日。放行則瓦礫生光。把住則真金失色。權柄在手殺活臨時。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the Continued Record of the Lamp (續傳燈錄), under the heirs of Zhimen Zuo, the speaker says: 'the treasury of the true eye of the teaching is entrusted here today; on releasing, tiles and rubble shine; on holding in place, true gold loses its color; authority is in hand, killing and giving life follow the occasion.' The immediate master name is not exposed by the rough head pointer, so no roster attribution is asserted.

Occurrences.Kwic: 今日打開布袋，放行一路，任汝諸人東跳西跳
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yinyuan Longqi's own record, in the Wanfu Chan Monastery at Mount Huangbo section. He says, 'today I open the cloth bag, open a road of release, and leave you all to jump east and west.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 把住即不問，如何是放行一句？」師云：「七通八達。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the Northern Travel Collection of Tiantong Hongjue Min (天童弘覺忞禪師北遊集), the question sets holding in place aside and asks for 'a saying of release'; the master answers, 'open in seven directions and reaching in eight.' Occurrences.Kwic: 且道。放行為人好。把住為人好。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu Keqin's own discourse record. He asks, 'say: is releasing good for people, or is holding in place good for people?' The text records the question without selecting either member here.

Occurrences.Kwic: 把定放行各出一隻手。扶竪宗乘。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wumen Huikai's comment under the public case headed 'Qianfeng's one road' (乾峯一路): 'holding fast and releasing each puts out one hand to raise the ancestral vehicle.' This is later case commentary, not speech attributed to either master in the encounter.
